questions.question: What is the simple definition of reproductive health according to the textbook?
options: Healthy reproductive organs with normal functions
Only physical well-being of reproductive organs
questions.explanation: The textbook states that reproductive health simply refers to healthy reproductive organs with normal functions.

questions.question: According to WHO, what does reproductive health mean?
options: Total well-being in all aspects of reproduction: physical, emotional, behavioural and social
questions.explanation: WHO defines reproductive health as total well-being in all aspects of reproduction, including physical, emotional, behavioural and social dimensions.

questions.question: Which country was among the first to initiate national-level action plans for reproductive health?
questions.explanation: India was amongst the first countries in the world to initiate action plans and programmes at a national level to attain total reproductive health as a social goal.

questions.question: When were family planning programmes initiated in India?
questions.explanation: Family planning programmes were initiated in India in 1951.

questions.question: What is the current popular name for improved programmes covering wider reproduction-related areas?
options: Reproductive and Child Health Care (RCH) programmes
questions.explanation: Improved programmes covering wider reproduction-related areas are currently in operation under the popular name 'Reproductive and Child Health Care (RCH) programmes'.

questions.question: What are the major tasks under RCH programmes?
options: Creating awareness and providing facilities for building a reproductively healthy society
questions.explanation: Creating awareness among people about various reproduction related aspects and providing facilities and support for building up a reproductively healthy society are the major tasks under RCH programmes.

questions.question: Which aspects of reproduction are included in the broader perspective of reproductive health?
questions.explanation: Reproductive health has a broader perspective and includes physical, emotional, behavioural and social aspects of reproduction.

questions.question: What is the significance of maintaining reproductive health in a society?
options: For total well-being in all aspects of reproduction
questions.explanation: Reproductive health is significant because it ensures total well-being in all aspects of reproduction, including physical, emotional, behavioural and social well-being.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a dimension of reproductive health according to WHO?
questions.explanation: According to WHO, reproductive health includes physical, emotional, behavioural and social aspects, but not economic aspects.

questions.question: What does a reproductively healthy society require according to the textbook?
options: Physically and functionally normal reproductive organs and normal emotional and behavioural interactions
questions.explanation: A society with people having physically and functionally normal reproductive organs and normal emotional and behavioural interactions among them in all sex-related aspects might be called reproductively healthy.

questions.question: What is the full form of RCH mentioned in the text?
questions.explanation: RCH stands for Reproductive and Child Health Care programmes.

questions.question: Which of the following is a method to achieve reproductive health mentioned in the text?
questions.explanation: Creating awareness among people about various reproduction related aspects is mentioned as a method to achieve reproductive health.

questions.question: What is the popular name for the improved programmes covering wider reproduction-related areas in India?
options: Reproductive and Child Health Care (RCH) Programmes
questions.explanation: The text states that improved programmes covering wider reproduction-related areas are currently in operation under the popular name 'Reproductive and Child Health Care (RCH) programmes'.

questions.question: Which of the following agencies help create awareness about reproduction-related aspects?
questions.explanation: The text mentions that with the help of audio-visual and print media, governmental and non-governmental agencies have taken various steps to create awareness among people about reproduction-related aspects.

questions.question: Who among the following have a major role in disseminating information about reproduction-related aspects?
questions.explanation: The text explicitly states that parents, other close relatives, teachers and friends also have a major role in the dissemination of information about reproduction-related aspects.

questions.question: Why should sex education be introduced in schools according to the text?
options: To provide right information and discourage myths and misconceptions
questions.explanation: The text states that introduction of sex education in schools should be encouraged to provide right information to the young so as to discourage children from believing in myths and having misconceptions about sex-related aspects.

questions.question: What topics should proper information about reproductive health cover?
options: Reproductive organs, adolescence, safe practices, STDs, AIDS
questions.explanation: The text mentions that proper information about reproductive organs, adolescence and related changes, safe and hygienic sexual practices, sexually transmitted diseases (STD), AIDS, etc. would help people lead a reproductively healthy life.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as something to educate people about in the marriageable age group?
options: Post-natal care of mother and child
questions.explanation: The text mentions educating people about birth control options, care of pregnant mothers, post-natal care of the mother and child, importance of breast feeding, and equal opportunities for male and female child. Space exploration is not mentioned.

questions.question: What is the purpose of creating awareness about uncontrolled population growth?
options: To enable people to take necessary steps to prevent problems and build a socially responsible society
questions.explanation: The text states that awareness of problems due to uncontrolled population growth needs to be created to enable people to think and take up necessary steps to prevent them and thereby build up a socially responsible and healthy society.

questions.question: What are the three essential requirements for successful implementation of reproductive health action plans?
options: Strong infrastructural facilities, professional expertise and material support
Political will, media support and public opinion
questions.explanation: The text explicitly states that successful implementation requires strong infrastructural facilities, professional expertise and material support. These are essential to provide medical assistance and care to people.

questions.question: What is amniocentesis used for according to the text?
options: Only for sex determination of the foetus
To test for certain genetic disorders and determine survivability of the foetus
questions.explanation: The text states that amniocentesis is used to test for the presence of certain genetic disorders such as Down syndrome, haemophilia, sickle-cell anemia, etc., and to determine the survivability of the foetus. The statutory ban is specifically for sex-determination.

questions.question: Which institution developed the oral contraceptive 'Saheli'?
options: Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI) in Lucknow
All India Institute of Medical Sciences
questions.explanation: The text mentions that 'Saheli' - a new oral contraceptive for females - was developed by scientists at Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI) in Lucknow, India.

questions.question: What does the text indicate about improved reproductive health in India?
options: Decreased maternal and infant mortality, increased small families, better STD detection, and increased medical facilities
questions.explanation: The text states that better awareness, increased medically assisted deliveries, better post-natal care leading to decreased maternal and infant mortality rates, increased couples with small families, better detection and cure of STDs, and overall increased medical facilities indicate improved reproductive health.

questions.question: What is the statutory ban mentioned in the text regarding amniocentesis?
options: Ban on all uses of amniocentesis
Ban on amniocentesis for sex-determination to check female foeticides
Ban on amniocentesis for genetic disorder testing
questions.explanation: The text mentions a statutory ban on amniocentesis for sex-determination to legally check the increasing menace of female foeticides. It does not ban amniocentesis for other legitimate medical purposes like genetic disorder testing.

questions.question: What was the world population in 1900 according to the textbook?
questions.explanation: The textbook states that the world population was around 2 billion (2000 million) in 1900.

questions.question: What was the world population in 2011 according to the textbook?
questions.explanation: The textbook mentions that the world population reached 7.2 billion in 2011.

questions.question: What was India's population at the time of independence?
questions.explanation: According to the textbook, India's population was approximately 350 million at the time of independence.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a probable reason for population explosion?
options: Increase in number of people in reproducible age
questions.explanation: The textbook mentions rapid decline in death rate, MMR, IMR and increase in reproducible age as reasons. Increase in literacy rate is not mentioned.

questions.question: What was the population growth rate according to the 2011 census report?
questions.explanation: The textbook states that according to the 2011 census, the population growth rate was less than 2 percent, i.e., 20/1000/year.

questions.question: What could be the consequence of alarming population growth rate?
options: Absolute scarcity of basic requirements like food, shelter and clothing
questions.explanation: The textbook warns that such alarming growth rate could lead to absolute scarcity of even basic requirements like food, shelter and clothing.

questions.question: What is the slogan used in advertisements to promote smaller families?
options: Hum Do Hamare Do (we two, our two)
questions.explanation: The textbook mentions the slogan 'Hum Do Hamare Do' (we two, our two) used in advertisements and posters showing a happy couple with two children.

questions.question: Which of the following is an ideal characteristic of a contraceptive method?
options: It should be user-friendly, easily available, effective and reversible with no or least side-effects
It should interfere with sexual drive and desire
It should be expensive and difficult to obtain
questions.explanation: The textbook states that an ideal contraceptive should be user-friendly, easily available, effective and reversible with no or least side-effects, and should not interfere with sexual drive or desire.

questions.question: Which natural contraceptive method involves avoiding coitus from day 10 to 17 of the menstrual cycle?
questions.explanation: Periodic abstinence is the method where couples avoid coitus from day 10 to 17 of the menstrual cycle when ovulation is expected. This period is called the fertile period.

questions.question: What is the maximum effective period for lactational amenorrhea as a contraceptive method?
questions.explanation: Lactational amenorrhea is effective only up to a maximum period of six months following parturition, as long as the mother fully breast-feeds the child.

questions.question: Which barrier method is made of thin rubber or latex sheath used to cover the penis?
questions.explanation: Male condoms are barriers made of thin rubber or latex sheath that are used to cover the penis before coitus to prevent semen from entering the female reproductive tract.

questions.question: Which of the following is a popular brand of male condom in India?
questions.explanation: Nirodh is mentioned in the textbook as a popular brand of condom for males in India.

questions.question: What additional benefit does condom use provide besides contraception?
questions.explanation: Use of condoms has increased due to its additional benefit of protecting the user from contracting sexually transmitted infections (STIs) and AIDS.

questions.question: Which barrier method is inserted into the female reproductive tract to cover the cervix during coitus?
questions.explanation: Diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults are barriers made of rubber that are inserted into the female reproductive tract to cover the cervix during coitus.

questions.question: Which type of IUD releases copper ions that suppress sperm motility?
questions.explanation: Copper releasing IUDs such as CuT, Cu7, and Multiload 375 release copper ions that suppress sperm motility and the fertilising capacity of sperms.

questions.question: Which IUD makes the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperms?
questions.explanation: Hormone releasing IUDs such as Progestasert and LNG-20 make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to the sperms.

questions.question: What mechanism do IUDs use to prevent conception?
options: They increase phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus
questions.explanation: IUDs increase phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus, and copper ions released suppress sperm motility and fertilising capacity.

questions.question: Which contraceptive method is ideal for females who want to delay pregnancy and space children?
questions.explanation: IUDs are ideal contraceptives for females who want to delay pregnancy and/or space children, and are one of the most widely accepted methods in India.

questions.question: Which of the following is a copper-releasing Intra Uterine Device (IUD)?
questions.explanation: CuT is a copper-releasing IUD. Lippes loop is a non-medicated IUD, while Progestasert and LNG-20 are hormone-releasing IUDs. Copper ions released from CuT suppress sperm motility and fertilising capacity.

questions.question: How do hormone-releasing IUDs prevent pregnancy?
options: By making the uterus unsuitable for implantation and cervix hostile to sperms
By blocking the fallopian tubes completely
questions.explanation: Hormone-releasing IUDs like Progestasert and LNG-20 make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to sperms. This dual action prevents pregnancy effectively.

questions.question: For how many days must oral contraceptive pills be taken continuously in one cycle?
questions.explanation: Oral contraceptive pills must be taken daily for a period of 21 days starting preferably within the first five days of the menstrual cycle. After a gap of 7 days (during which menstruation occurs), the cycle is repeated.

questions.question: What is the unique feature of 'Saheli' oral contraceptive?
options: It is a once-a-week pill with very few side effects
It must be taken daily for 28 days
questions.explanation: Saheli is a new oral contraceptive developed by scientists at CDRI Lucknow, India. It contains a non-steroidal preparation and is a 'once a week' pill with very few side effects and high contraceptive value.

questions.question: What is the time limit for using emergency contraceptives after unprotected coitus?
questions.explanation: Administration of progestogens or progestogen-estrogen combinations or IUDs within 72 hours of coitus have been found to be very effective as emergency contraceptives. They can be used to avoid possible pregnancy due to rape or casual unprotected intercourse.

questions.question: In a vasectomy procedure, which structure is tied and cut?
questions.explanation: In vasectomy, a small part of the vas deferens is removed or tied up through a small incision on the scrotum. This is the male sterilisation procedure that blocks gamete transport.

questions.question: Which surgical method is used for female sterilisation?
questions.explanation: Tubectomy is the sterilisation procedure in the female where a small part of the fallopian tube is removed or tied up through a small incision in the abdomen or through vagina. It blocks gamete transport and prevents conception.

questions.question: What is the main disadvantage of surgical sterilisation methods?
questions.explanation: Surgical methods like vasectomy and tubectomy are highly effective in preventing conception, but their reversibility is very poor. Once performed, it is extremely difficult to restore fertility.

questions.question: Which of the following is a non-medicated IUD?
questions.explanation: Lippes loop is a non-medicated IUD. CuT, Cu7, and Multiload 375 are copper-releasing IUDs. Non-medicated IUDs work primarily by increasing phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus.

questions.question: How do copper-releasing IUDs affect sperm function?
options: They suppress sperm motility and fertilising capacity
They block sperm production in testes
questions.explanation: Copper-releasing IUDs like CuT, Cu7, and Multiload 375 release Cu ions that suppress sperm motility and the fertilising capacity of sperms. This prevents fertilisation from occurring.

questions.question: What happens during the 7-day gap in the oral contraceptive pill cycle?
options: The woman takes a different medication
The pills are stored for next cycle
questions.explanation: After taking pills for 21 days, there is a gap of 7 days during which menstruation occurs. Then the 21-day pill cycle is repeated in the same pattern until the female desires to prevent conception.

questions.question: Which mechanism is NOT involved in the action of oral contraceptive pills?
questions.explanation: Oral pills inhibit ovulation and implantation as well as alter the quality of cervical mucus to prevent or retard entry of sperms. They do NOT destroy sperm in the vagina.

questions.question: Progestogens can be administered as contraceptives through which routes?
questions.explanation: Progestogens alone or in combination with estrogen can be used by females as oral pills, injections, or implants under the skin. Their mode of action is similar to that of pills but their effective periods are much longer.

questions.question: Who are IUDs most suitable for?
options: Women who want to delay pregnancy and/or space children
questions.explanation: IUDs are ideal contraceptives for females who want to delay pregnancy and/or space children. It is one of the most widely accepted methods of contraception in India.

questions.question: What type of preparation does 'Saheli' contain?
questions.explanation: Saheli contains a non-steroidal preparation. This is different from most other oral contraceptives which contain steroidal hormones (progestogens or progestogen-estrogen combinations).

questions.question: What is the full form of MTP?
questions.explanation: MTP stands for Medical Termination of Pregnancy, which refers to intentional or voluntary termination of pregnancy before full term.

questions.question: How many MTPs are performed in a year all over the world approximately?
questions.explanation: Nearly 45 to 50 million MTPs are performed in a year all over the world, which accounts to 1/5th of the total number of conceived pregnancies in a year.

questions.question: When was MTP legalised in India?
questions.explanation: Government of India legalised MTP in 1971 with some strict conditions to avoid its misuse.

questions.question: What fraction of total conceived pregnancies result in MTPs annually worldwide?
questions.explanation: MTPs account to 1/5th of the total number of conceived pregnancies in a year worldwide.

questions.question: Why are MTPs performed?
options: To get rid of unwanted pregnancies due to casual unprotected intercourse, failure of contraceptives, or rapes
questions.explanation: MTPs are performed to get rid of unwanted pregnancies either due to casual unprotected intercourse or failure of the contraceptive used during coitus or rapes.

questions.question: During which trimester are MTPs considered relatively safe?
questions.explanation: MTPs are considered relatively safe during the first trimester, i.e., upto 12 weeks of pregnancy. Second trimester abortions are much more riskier.

questions.question: What is a disturbing trend observed in MTPs?
options: All MTPs are performed by qualified doctors
A majority of MTPs are performed illegally by unqualified quacks
MTPs are never performed in India
MTPs are only done in government hospitals
questions.explanation: One disturbing trend observed is that a majority of the MTPs are performed illegally by unqualified quacks which are not only unsafe but could be fatal too.

questions.question: What is the dangerous misuse of amniocentesis mentioned in the text?
options: To determine the sex of the unborn child followed by MTP if female
To check the health of the mother
To determine the blood type of the foetus
questions.explanation: Another dangerous trend is the misuse of amniocentesis to determine the sex of the unborn child. Frequently, if the foetus is found to be female, it is followed by MTP - this is totally against what is ethical.

questions.question: What is the maximum safe period for MTP in weeks?
questions.explanation: MTPs are considered relatively safe during the first trimester, i.e., upto 12 weeks of pregnancy.

questions.question: What are the complications of illegal abortions?
options: They are safe and have no complications
They are unsafe and could be fatal
questions.explanation: A majority of MTPs are performed illegally by unqualified quacks which are not only unsafe but could be fatal too.

questions.question: What does the text say about MTPs in cases where continuation of pregnancy is harmful?
options: MTPs are essential when continuation of pregnancy could be harmful or fatal to mother or foetus
MTPs are only allowed for economic reasons
MTPs are banned in all cases
questions.explanation: MTPs are also essential in certain cases where continuation of the pregnancy could be harmful or even fatal either to the mother or to the foetus or both.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the strict conditions imposed on MTP in India?
options: To avoid misuse of MTP and check indiscriminate female foeticides
To promote MTP for all pregnancies
questions.explanation: Government of India legalised MTP in 1971 with some strict conditions to avoid its misuse. Such restrictions are all the more important to check indiscriminate and illegal female foeticides.

questions.question: What is the term for spontaneous abortion?
options: The text mentions abortions could happen spontaneously too
questions.explanation: The text mentions that abortions could happen spontaneously too, which refers to natural miscarriage without medical intervention.

questions.question: What counselling is suggested to avoid unhealthy trends in MTP?
options: Counselling on the need to avoid unprotected coitus and risk factors in illegal abortions
questions.explanation: Effective counselling on the need to avoid unprotected coitus and the risk factors involved in illegal abortions as well as providing more health care facilities could reverse the mentioned unhealthy trends.

questions.question: What is the main reason for legalising MTP according to the text?
options: To get rid of unwanted pregnancies and protect maternal health
questions.explanation: MTP is legalised to get rid of unwanted pregnancies and in cases where continuation of pregnancy could be harmful or fatal to the mother or foetus.

questions.question: What is the risk associated with second trimester abortions?
options: They are safer than first trimester
They are much more riskier than first trimester abortions
They are only done in emergencies
questions.explanation: Second trimester abortions are much more riskier compared to first trimester abortions.

questions.question: What is the relationship between amniocentesis and female foeticide mentioned in the text?
options: Amniocentesis is used to promote female births
Amniocentesis is misused to determine sex and if female, MTP is performed
Amniocentesis has no relation to female foeticide
Amniocentesis is banned for all purposes
questions.explanation: The text mentions that amniocentesis is misused to determine the sex of the unborn child, and if the foetus is found to be female, it is followed by MTP. This is totally against what is ethical.

questions.question: What are the two main reasons for MTP mentioned in the text?
options: Only for rape cases and contraceptive failure
Unwanted pregnancies and harmful continuation of pregnancy
questions.explanation: MTPs are performed to get rid of unwanted pregnancies and in cases where continuation of pregnancy could be harmful or fatal to mother or foetus.

questions.question: What is the ethical concern regarding misuse of amniocentesis?
options: It leads to female foeticide which is totally against ethics
It causes pain to the mother
questions.explanation: The misuse of amniocentesis for sex determination leading to female foeticide is totally against what is ethical.

questions.question: What measures can reverse unhealthy trends in MTP?
options: Counselling, avoiding unprotected coitus, and providing more healthcare facilities
questions.explanation: Effective counselling on avoiding unprotected coitus, awareness about risk factors in illegal abortions, and providing more healthcare facilities could reverse unhealthy trends.

questions.question: What are infections transmitted through sexual intercourse collectively called?
questions.explanation: Infections or diseases transmitted through sexual intercourse are collectively called sexually transmitted infections (STI) or venereal diseases (VD) or reproductive tract infections (RTI).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a common sexually transmitted infection mentioned in the text?
questions.explanation: Gonorrhoea, syphilis, genital herpes, chlamydiasis, genital warts, trichomoniasis, hepatitis-B and HIV are mentioned as common STIs. Tuberculosis is not a sexually transmitted infection.

questions.question: Which STI is described as the most dangerous in recent years?
questions.explanation: Among the common STIs, HIV infection is most dangerous and is discussed in detail. It is the most discussed infection in recent years.

questions.question: Which of the following STIs can be transmitted through sharing of injection needles?
questions.explanation: Some infections like hepatitis-B and HIV can also be transmitted by sharing of injection needles, surgical instruments, transfusion of blood, or from an infected mother to the foetus.

questions.question: Which STIs are completely curable if detected early and treated properly?
options: All except hepatitis-B, genital herpes and HIV
questions.explanation: Except for hepatitis-B, genital herpes and HIV infections, other diseases are completely curable if detected early and treated properly.

questions.question: What are the early symptoms of most STIs?
options: Itching, fluid discharge, slight pain, swellings in the genital region
questions.explanation: Early symptoms of most STIs are minor and include itching, fluid discharge, slight pain, swellings, etc., in the genital region.

questions.question: Why do infected females often remain undetected for long?
options: Because they may often be asymptomatic
Because STIs do not affect females
questions.explanation: Infected females may often be asymptomatic and hence, may remain undetected for long.

questions.question: What complications can arise from untreated STIs?
options: PID, abortions, still births, ectopic pregnancies, infertility, cancer of reproductive tract
questions.explanation: Complications of untreated STIs include pelvic inflammatory diseases (PID), abortions, still births, ectopic pregnancies, infertility or even cancer of the reproductive tract.

questions.question: Which age group has the highest reported incidence of STIs?
questions.explanation: The incidences of STIs are reported to be very high among persons in the age group of 15-24 years.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended precaution to avoid contracting STIs?
options: Go to a qualified doctor for early detection
questions.explanation: Recommended precautions include avoiding sex with unknown/multiple partners, using condoms, and going to a qualified doctor for early detection. Sharing needles is a mode of transmission, not a precaution.

questions.question: What is the definition of infertility?
options: Inability to produce children despite unprotected sexual co-habitation
questions.explanation: Infertility is defined as the inability to produce children in spite of unprotected sexual co-habitation.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a cause of infertility?
questions.explanation: The reasons for infertility could be physical, congenital, diseases, drugs, immunological or even psychological. Dietary habits are not mentioned as a cause.

questions.question: What is the popular name for the IVF technique?
questions.explanation: In vitro fertilisation (IVF) followed by embryo transfer is popularly known as test tube baby programme.

questions.question: In ZIFT, where is the zygote or early embryo transferred?
questions.explanation: ZIFT (zygote intra fallopian transfer) involves transferring the zygote or early embryos (with upto 8 blastomeres) into the fallopian tube.

questions.question: What does ICSI stand for?
questions.explanation: ICSI stands for Intra Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection, a specialised procedure where a sperm is directly injected into the ovum.

questions.question: What is the full form of GIFT?
questions.explanation: GIFT stands for Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer, where an ovum from a donor is transferred into the fallopian tube of another female.

questions.question: In artificial insemination (AI), where is the semen introduced?
options: Either into the vagina or into the uterus (IUI)
questions.explanation: In artificial insemination (AI), the semen is artificially introduced either into the vagina or into the uterus (IUI - intra-uterine insemination).

questions.question: What is one of the best methods for couples looking for children in India according to the text?
options: Legal adoption of orphaned and destitute children
questions.explanation: The text mentions that legal adoption of orphaned and destitute children is one of the best methods for couples looking for children, as there are many such children who need care.

questions.question: What is the definition of infertility according to the textbook?
options: Inability to produce children despite protected sexual co-habitation
Inability to produce children despite unprotected sexual co-habitation
Inability to produce children due to genetic disorders only
Inability to produce children after one year of marriage
questions.explanation: Infertility is defined as the inability to produce children inspite of unprotected sexual co-habitation.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a cause of infertility in the textbook?
questions.explanation: The textbook mentions physical, congenital, diseases, drugs, immunological and psychological factors as causes of infertility. Nutritional deficiency is not mentioned.

questions.question: According to the textbook, who is often blamed for infertility in India?
questions.explanation: In India, often the female is blamed for the couple being childless, but more often than not, the problem lies in the male partner.

questions.question: What does IVF stand for in assisted reproductive technology?
questions.explanation: IVF stands for In vitro Fertilisation, which means fertilisation outside the body in almost similar conditions as that in the body.

questions.question: What is the popular name for the IVF followed by embryo transfer programme?
questions.explanation: The method of IVF followed by embryo transfer is popularly known as the test tube baby programme.

questions.question: In ZIFT, where is the zygote or early embryo transferred?
questions.explanation: In ZIFT (Zygote Intra Fallopian Transfer), the zygote or early embryos with upto 8 blastomeres are transferred into the fallopian tube.

questions.question: What is the full form of IUT mentioned in the textbook?
questions.explanation: IUT stands for Intra Uterine Transfer, where embryos with more than 8 blastomeres are transferred into the uterus.

questions.question: What does GIFT stand for in assisted reproductive technology?
questions.explanation: GIFT stands for Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer, where an ovum from a donor is transferred into the fallopian tube of another female.

questions.question: What is ICSI in the context of assisted reproductive technology?
options: Injecting sperm directly into the ovum
Injecting ovum into the fallopian tube
Injecting hormones into the female body
questions.explanation: ICSI (Intra Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection) is a specialised procedure where a sperm is directly injected into the ovum.

questions.question: What is artificial insemination (AI) technique used for?
options: For sex determination of the fetus
For correcting infertility due to inability of male partner to inseminate or low sperm counts
questions.explanation: Artificial insemination (AI) is used to correct infertility cases due to inability of the male partner to inseminate the female or due to very low sperm counts in the ejaculates.

questions.question: What does IUI stand for?
questions.explanation: IUI stands for Intra Uterine Insemination, where semen is artificially introduced into the uterus.

questions.question: Why are assisted reproductive technologies available only in very few centres in India?
options: Because they are banned by the government
Because they require extremely high precision handling and expensive instrumentation
Because they are only for foreign patients
questions.explanation: These techniques require extremely high precision handling by specialised professionals and expensive instrumentation, making them available only in very few centres.

questions.question: Which of the following is mentioned as a deterrent in the adoption of assisted reproductive technologies?
questions.explanation: Emotional, religious and social factors are mentioned as deterrents in the adoption of these methods.

questions.question: What alternative solution does the textbook suggest for couples looking to have children when ART is not possible?
questions.explanation: The textbook mentions that legal adoption is one of the best methods for couples looking for children, as there are many orphaned and destitute children in India.

questions.question: Where are embryos with more than 8 blastomeres transferred according to the textbook?
questions.explanation: Embryos with more than 8 blastomeres are transferred into the uterus through IUT (Intra Uterine Transfer).

questions.question: According to the textbook, what does reproductive health refer to?
options: Total well-being in physical, emotional, behavioural and social aspects of reproduction
questions.explanation: Reproductive health refers to a total well-being in all aspects of reproduction, i.e., physical, emotional, behavioural and social.

questions.question: Which country was the first in the world to initiate action plans at national level for reproductive health?
questions.explanation: Our nation (India) was the first nation in the world to initiate various action plans at national level towards attaining a reproductively healthy society.

questions.question: What is the primary step towards reproductive health according to the textbook?
options: Counselling and creating awareness about reproductive organs, adolescence, safe practices, and STIs
questions.explanation: Counselling and creating awareness among people about reproductive organs, adolescence and associated changes, safe and hygienic sexual practices, sexually transmitted infections (STIs) including AIDS, etc., is the primary step towards reproductive health.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a problem addressed by Reproductive and Child Health Care programmes?
questions.explanation: The textbook mentions menstrual irregularities, pregnancy related aspects, delivery, medical termination of pregnancy, STIs, birth control, infertility, post natal child and maternal management. Common cold is not mentioned.

questions.question: What indicates overall improvement in reproductive health in our country?
options: Reduced maternal and infant mortality rates, early detection and cure of STIs, assistance to infertile couples
questions.explanation: An overall improvement in reproductive health has taken place as indicated by reduced maternal and infant mortality rates, early detection and cure of STIs, assistance to infertile couples, etc.

questions.question: What promoted the explosive growth of population according to the textbook?
options: Improved health facilities and better living conditions
questions.explanation: Improved health facilities and better living conditions promoted an explosive growth of population.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as a contraceptive option in the textbook?
questions.explanation: The textbook lists natural, traditional, barrier, IUDs, pills, injectables, implants and surgical methods as contraceptive options. Radiation therapy is not mentioned.

questions.question: Are contraceptives regular requirements for reproductive health?
options: Yes, they are essential daily requirements
No, they are not regular requirements but used to avoid, delay or space pregnancy
questions.explanation: Though contraceptives are not regular requirements for reproductive health, one is forced to use them to avoid pregnancy or to delay or space pregnancy.

questions.question: Is medical termination of pregnancy legalised in India?
options: Yes, it is legalised in our country
questions.explanation: Medical termination of pregnancy is legalised in our country.

questions.question: For which reasons is MTP generally performed according to the textbook?
options: To get rid of unwanted pregnancy due to rapes, casual relationships, or when continuation is harmful/fatal
questions.explanation: MTP is generally performed to get rid of unwanted pregnancy due to rapes, casual relationship, etc., as also in cases when the continuation of pregnancy could be harmful or even fatal to either the mother, or the foetus or both.

questions.question: What are infections or diseases transmitted through sexual intercourse called?
questions.explanation: Infections or diseases transmitted through sexual intercourse are called Sexually Transmitted Diseases (STIs).

questions.question: Which of the following is mentioned as a complication of STIs?
options: Pelvic Inflammatory Diseases (PIDs), still birth, infertility
questions.explanation: Pelvic Inflammatory Diseases (PIDs), still birth, infertility are some of the complications of STIs.

questions.question: What facilitates better cure of STIs?
questions.explanation: Early detection facilitate better cure of these diseases.

questions.question: Which of the following is mentioned as a simple precaution to avoid contracting STIs?
options: Avoiding sexual intercourse with unknown/multiple partners and use of condoms during coitus
Complete abstinence from all social activities
questions.explanation: Avoiding sexual intercourse with unknown/multiple partners, use of condoms during coitus are some of the simple precautions to avoid contracting STIs.

questions.question: How is infertility defined in the textbook?
options: Inability to conceive after 6 months of marriage
Inability to conceive or produce children even after 2 years of unprotected sexual cohabitation
questions.explanation: Inability to conceive or produce children even after 2 years of unprotected sexual cohabitation is called infertility.

questions.question: What is the 'Test Tube Baby' Programme?
options: In Vitro fertilisation followed by transfer of embryo into the female genital tract
questions.explanation: In Vitro fertilisation followed by transfer of embryo into the female genital tract is commonly known as the 'Test Tube Baby' Programme.
